- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to match bearish trend.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points above peak if sentiment remains neutral or slightly bullish.  
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if recent 10-day average is 10%+ above 30-day average, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to reflect reversion.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting — apply a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast upward slope.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “sustained breakout” heuristic: add 0.5–1.5% to next forecast to account for momentum.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — use 3-day moving average of true price as baseline for adjustment.
